mechanism_narrative: A sharp concurrent decline in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES signals fewer trips to dense activity nodes, which reduces incidental shopping and dining visits. If that contraction persists, RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks than over the last four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not stay below its prior 4-week mean during the next 28 days even while TRANSIT and WORKPLACES remain depressed relative to t-3w.

mechanism_narrative: When RESIDENTIAL rises above 12 percentage points, people substitute away from discretionary outings into staying home, and retail visits fall within one week. That homebound shift will pull RETAIL_REC down over the next week.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL is 14.7 at t-0w and has risen for four consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 7 days after RESIDENTIAL stays above 12 points and instead rebounds toward its prior 4-week average.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rebound in GROCERY_PHARM and stabilization of TRANSIT indicates essential-trip activity is replacing discretionary foot traffic. That pattern predicts a further fall in retail and recreation demand over the next two weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises or holds flat over the next 14 days while GROCERY_PHARM remains elevated and TRANSIT does not recover.

mechanism_narrative: A deepening negative PARKS reading marks weak outdoor leisure demand and poor weekend discretionary activity. Because park use leads shopping by roughly one month in this setting, RETAIL_REC will be lower over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not underperform its previous 4-week average over the next 28 days despite PARKS staying markedly negative.

mechanism_narrative: If TRANSIT falls by more than 10 points week-on-week while WORKPLACES also declines, the combined signal indicates mobility restrictions or avoidance behavior that directly suppresses shopping trips. Retail and recreation will be lower within two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT falls > 10 points week-on-week and WORKPLACES also declines
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT dropped from -20.7 to -31.9 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not fall within 14 days after a further weekly drop in TRANSIT paired with declining WORKPLACES.

mechanism_narrative: A steady rise in RESIDENTIAL alongside falling WORKPLACES captures substitution toward staying home and away from discretionary stops. That behavior lowers retail traffic over the next four weeks rather than immediately.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC is not lower over the next 28 days even though RESIDENTIAL keeps rising and WORKPLACES keeps falling.

mechanism_narrative: When both PARKS and TRANSIT are below their recent levels for two straight weeks, the city is in a broad mobility suppression regime that spills into nonessential shopping. RETAIL_REC will continue to weaken over the next week and a half.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and TRANSIT remain below their prior week values for 2 consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to decline within 7 to 10 days after two consecutive weeks of low PARKS and low TRANSIT.

mechanism_narrative: If GROCERY_PHARM stops falling and begins to recover while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated, the shift from crisis-style essentials to localized neighborhood activity will support retail visits after a short lag. RETAIL_REC will turn higher over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM stops declining and turns upward while RESIDENTIAL stays above 10 points
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM moved from 21.6 to -5.3 across the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise within 14 days after GROCERY_PHARM reverses upward while RESIDENTIAL remains elevated.
